rated_messages.input_message: See what it is like to let the urge pass. You can have an urge and choose not to smoke.
You spent a long time training your brain to want a cig. Now you're retraining your brain, and it's natural that this might take time.
Some people find that having a simple mantra can really help, especially if things feel stressful. Try repeating something simple to yourself like: "I can do it!".
How you would feel later on if you smoked during this social situation? Now think how good you'll feel for resisting!
Urges are like annoying ads. You might see them but you don't have to buy what they're selling.
Take a slow, deep breath in. And let it out. Now, ask yourself, "Am I willing to go one minute without smoking?" When that minute is over, ask yourself this question again.
Feelings aren't permanent. They are always changing like the weather. Observe the storm that is coming, but don't fight it. Eventually the weather will change.
You might find that you have more time now that you're trying to cut some cigarettes. Some people find that going for a walk can help fill the gap. Or take a nap if you can!

Now is a good time for BREAKS B=stop and Brake R=Read how your body feels E=Expand and take deep breaths A=Allow everything to be as it is K=Know what's important to you S=take 1 Step in a direction important to you
When you begin to crave a cig, concentrate on your reasons for not smoking. Keep a list on your phone and look at it when you feel yourself beginning to falter.
